articles.title: ‘American History X’ Director Tony Kaye Takes On Leicester’s Giant Monsters in Short ‘Will You Still Love Me Tomorrow?’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Tony Kaye, the British director of “American History X” and “Detachment,” will direct “Will You Still Love Me Tomorrow?,” a short running five minutes that blends documentary with reality drama and plays out among the giant monster sculptures installed across Leicester, England.
body: The narrative will take shape around the chosen cast and participants, with the camera catching chance encounters and real human experiences as the film asks whether people can come to understand and love each other across their differences. The shoot commences on Friday. Louis Lingjaerde (“Vipers”) is the cinematographer.

The short will take its setting from Leicester Monsters, a downtown program run by BID Leicester that has placed oversized creatures on the city’s streets and in its public spaces to coax visitors into exploring the center. Bristol-based Designs in Air installed the monsters.

“Forty years ago, I made a commercial for solid fuel in which a dog, a cat and a mouse kissed each other in front of a real coal fire, to the music of ‘Will You Still Love Me Tomorrow.’ I’ve never forgotten that image,” Kaye said. “Now, with the Leicester Monsters movie, I find myself returning to the same idea. Perhaps the universe is the real coal fire, and we are all just animals gathered around it, trying to work out how to love one another. The question is as simple as it is impossible: how can we all get along, forever?”

articles.title: Microdrama Platform FlareFlow Sets Thailand Launch on AIS Play (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Microdrama platform FlareFlow will launch in Thailand on Nov. 2 through AIS Play, the entertainment service of Thai telecom operator Advanced Info Service (AIS), in a deal brokered by Singapore-based distributor Rock Networks.
body: Romance, drama, fantasy and reality shows feature in the lineup, alongside a selection of LGBTQ+ titles.

Launch titles include the English-language “From Janitor to Mrs Billionaire,” the Chinese-language “Rise of Aurora’s Fallen General” and the Korean Boys’ Love series “My Team Leader Is Working Late Again.” Also on the slate is “SupermodelMe: Make It or Break It,” a reality contest franchise shot in vertical format and fronted by Thai TV personality, actor and model Cindy Bishop.

“Thailand is one of Southeast Asia’s most creative, connected and culturally influential entertainment markets,” said Timothy Oh, general manager of COL Group International and chief marketing officer of FlareFlow. “Our launch with AIS Play is about making premium vertical entertainment accessible to more Thai audiences. At THB39 per month, viewers will be able to discover thousands of mobile-first stories backed by the scale, content library and industry experience of COL Group.”

articles.title: Oh to Believe in Another World review – William Kentridge’s amazing animated ballet of black comic pain
articles.summary: Kentridge’s cine-musical creation, made to accompany Shostakovich’s 10th Symphony, is a marvel of puppetry, dance and humour, exploring humanity, grief and idealism. The Baku international arts festival in Azerbaijan is showcasing an amazing cine-musical creation, perhaps the most amazing animation…
body: My colleague Jonathan Jones has written about Kentridge’s film but what I hadn’t anticipated was how funny it is: the simple, preposterous effect of seeing Stalin’s great big monumental face on top of a dancer’s body, and seeing that face remain unchanged despite the exertions below, staring resolutely ahead at the far horizon of history. It is hilarious, a little like Terry Gilliam’s animations for Monty Python. But is it supposed to be funny? Chaplin showed that the way to defy Hitler was to laugh at him. Kentridge (and Kentridge’s Shostakovich) are doing something similar with Stalin but not exactly the same. It is a ballet of black comic pain.

articles.title: Mohammad Rasoulof, Shahrbanoo Sadat Push Back on Idea of Separate Oscar Category for Exiled Filmmakers as Cate Blanchett’s Displacement Film Fund Hits Tokyo
articles.summary: Iranian filmmaker Mohammad Rasoulof and Iranian-born Afghan director Shahrbanoo Sadat pushed back on the idea of a standalone Oscar category for exiled filmmakers, speaking at the Tokyo International Film Festival as Cate Blanchett’s Displacement Film Fund gave its first five short films their…
body: “I really do not like to be labeled, and even this label is displaced, you know, because I’m not seeing myself like I’m Shahrbanoo Sadat, the displaced filmmaker. This is funny, this is a joke to me,” said Sadat, whose fund-backed short is “Super Afghan Gym.” “I’m not sure if I would love to be in the category of displaced, even if they give me the Oscar.”

Rasoulof, who directed the fund’s “The Sense of Water,” said that as a filmmaker he wanted to put all his energy into making films, and that from that point of view it might not matter much where they are shown. “If there are certain specific categories, then sometimes those could cause an issue, so I would really like to focus my efforts on closing the distance and being closer,” he said.

Clare Stewart, managing director of International Film Festival Rotterdam (IFFR), whose Hubert Bals Fund manages the Displacement Film Fund, pointed out that Rasoulof’s own “The Seed of the Sacred Fig,” nominated in the last Oscar cycle, was one of the first films to benefit from the change, and that it represented Germany.

articles.title: Annecy Winner ‘The Violinist’ Found Its Italian Co-Producers at Tokyo Market, Director Ervin Han Tells Anime Co-Production Panel
articles.summary: A meeting at TIFFCOM in 2023 brought Italian co-producers to “The Violinist,” the animated feature that went on to win the top prize at France’s Annecy International Animation Film Festival this year, Singaporean filmmaker Ervin Han told a panel at the Tokyo market.
body: Han co-directed and produced “The Violinist.” On his first TIFFCOM visit, he met Italian producer Cristiano Bortone and his team at Altri Occhi, who later joined the film as co-producers. This year, Han returned as producer to pitch “A Banquet for Hungry Ghosts,” an animated feature about food, horror and temptation, with partners from Singapore, Taiwan, Malaysia and Ireland.

Han described “The Violinist” as a story of friendship over a decade. The film itself also took 10 years from conception to completion. “With different roles in my projects, I find promotion is even more challenging than production,” he said.

articles.title: Sir Ian McKellen leads tributes to 'beloved actor' Sir Patrick Stewart after his death at 86
articles.summary: The actor died in Los Angeles following a "a brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.
body: Sir Ian McKellen has led tributes to Sir Patrick Stewart following his death at the age of 86, calling him "the most respected and beloved actor of his generation".
"He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and, in my case, love," Sir Ian, Sir Patrick's X-Men co-star, said.
Famous for his role as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek, Sir Patrick was a versatile actor who won multiple awards, balancing Hollywood roles and a career in classical theatre.
William Shatner, who also helmed the USS Enterprise in Star Trek, said Sir Patrick brought "intelligence, grace and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did".
points: The actor died in Los Angeles following a "a brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.

articles.title: Sir Patrick Stewart: A life in pictures
articles.summary: His career on stages and screens spanned seven decades but came to be defined by his roles on some of the most popular sci-fi franchises in history.
body: The star, who won acclaim on both stages and screens, died at his home in Los Angeles on Thursday after a career that spanned more than seven decades. He was 86.
Born in 1940, his mother was a textile worker and his father was a former military officer whose experience during the wartime evacuation of Dunkirk had a profound impact on his mental health.
He grew up poor, and later spoke to journalists about witnessing his mother being abused by his father.
Young Patrick's love of drama came at school when one of his teachers introduced him to Shakespeare and encouraged him to perform.

body: The 30th anniversary edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival ( PÖFF ) is kicking off on Nov. 6, screening all sorts of art house world premieres, new discoveries and highlights from the festival circuit of the past year.
Movies from the Baltic region, Europe, Asia and beyond will screen in the Estonian capital and look to create buzz.

articles.title: Ex-Traitors players talk tactics and celebrity final predictions
articles.summary: Former contestants share their thoughts on life in the castle ahead of Friday's final.
body: Spoiler warning: This article reveals details from episode nine of The Celebrity Traitors, series two.

From shock slip-ups to a murder by yawning - and a whole host of Jerry Hall one-liners along the way - the current series of Celebrity Traitors has gripped the nation. But ahead of Friday's finale, what do former contestants make of this season's crop of stars and who are they tipping to win?
Judy, from Doncaster, took home the unwanted title of the first player to be banished from the castle in series four.
She told the BBC while it was a shame people didn't get to see more of her personality, she knew her daughter and fellow player, Roxy, would be "fighting for both of us".
